So marker causes projection in direction perpendicular? Marker located within horizontal rectangular object, extends upward as strip of same width? The object height 2, marker near top? Wait marker at top row of right object. Direction is upward (since marker at top edge? Actually right object rows7-8; marker at r7, top row, c7 middle). Output extends upward from top row, making vertical column of width? The original right object width 5. Why added width 3 cols6-8? Because marker column c7 with one cell left/right? In row7 original c5-c9 all 3 except c7=2. Projection upward uses columns c6-c8: center marker col7 plus adjacent 1 each side? Why not full width c5-c9? Maybe due to object width/height? Ex2 left marker at (2,1), object rows1-2 cols0-3. Marker is at bottom row? r2 bottom row, col1. Direction down. Output added rows3-9 at cols0-2? Wait center column c1=2, side cols c0 and c2 =3. That is width 3 centered at c1 extending downward from row2 to bottom. Yes exactly. It fills c1=2 for rows3-9, c0=3,c2=3. row3 output [3,2,3,...] etc. Good.

Ex2 right marker at (8,6), object rows4-9 cols5-6. Marker at bottom row? r8 near bottom? Actually object rows4-9, marker row8, not bottom (r9 below). Hmm direction? Output added to right: rows7-9?
